record.paper_title: Open Problems in Universal Induction & Intelligence
record.original_question: Which mathematically precise intelligence-related properties—such as creativity, problem solving, pattern recognition, classification, learning, induction, deduction, building analogies, optimization, surviving in an environment, language processing, and planning—does AIXI satisfy as a rational agent?

evidence.quote: d) Intelligence Aspects of AIXI. Intelligence can have many faces. As argued in [Hut05], it is plausible that AIXI possesses all or at least most properties an intelligent rational agent should posses. Some of the following properties could and should be investigated mathematically: creativity, problem solving, pattern recognition, classification, learning, induction, deduction, building analogies, optimization, surviving in an environment, language processing, planning.

artifact.self_contained_problem:
Let AIXI denote the universal reinforcement-learning agent defined as follows. Fix a finite action set A, a finite percept set E = O × R where O is a set of observations and R ⊂ ℚ ∩ [0,1] is a finite set of rewards. For an interaction history of length t, write a_{1:t} = a_1 a_2 … a_t and e_{1:t} = e_1 e_2 … e_t with e_k = (o_k, r_k). Let M be the class of all lower semi-computable chronological semimeasures over (A × E)^∞, and let ξ(e_{1:t} ‖ a_{1:t}) := Σ_{ν∈M} 2^{-K(ν)} ν(e_{1:t} ‖ a_{1:t}) be the universal Solomonoff–Hutter mixture, where K(·) denotes prefix Kolmogorov complexity. For a fixed lifetime m ≥ 1 and discount γ_k ≥ 0 with Σγ_k < ∞, define AIXI by

  a_t^{AIXI} := arg max_{a_t} Σ_{e_t} … max_{a_m} Σ_{e_m} (Σ_{k=t}^{m} γ_k r_k) ξ(e_{1:m} ‖ a_{1:m}),

acting at every time step t given the past history a_{<t} e_{<t}.

Provide mathematically precise formal definitions, within this framework, of each of the following intelligence-related properties of an agent — (i) creativity, (ii) problem solving, (iii) pattern recognition, (iv) classification, (v) learning, (vi) induction, (vii) deduction, (viii) building analogies, (ix) optimization, (x) surviving in an environment, (xi) language processing, (xii) planning — and, for each property, prove or disprove that AIXI satisfies it as a rational agent.
artifact.status_search_result: No formal mathematical results are known that systematically establish (or refute) such intelligence-related properties of AIXI. Subsequent work on AIXI has focused on optimality notions (Pareto/self-optimizing), legg–Hutter universal intelligence, asymptotic non-learnability results (Leike & Hutter), and variants such as AIXI_tl and BayesExp, but the listed properties (creativity, analogy-building, language processing, etc.) have not received agreed-upon formal definitions or proofs in the AIXI framework.

status_evidence.title: Open Problems in Universal Induction & Intelligence
status_evidence.snippet: Lists intelligence aspects of AIXI (creativity, problem solving, pattern recognition, ... planning) as properties that 'could and should be investigated mathematically'.
status_evidence.claim: The problem is posed as an open research direction rather than a resolved question.
